mainTopic: The Temple song (voice or instruments), the dispute over the Water Drawing music on שבת, and the משנה describing שמחת בית השואבה
overview: The גמרא first tries to find the argument over whether the Temple song is mainly the voice (בפה) or the instruments (בכלי) in a dispute of תנאים. That dispute is about who played the instruments: slaves of כהנים, distinguished Israelite families, or לוים. רבי יוסי's middle view fits neither side, so the גמרא concludes that everyone holds עיקר שירה בפה. The תנאים only disagree about what actually happened. That historical fact matters for whether playing on the דוכן proves pure lineage and the right to מעשר. Next, רבי ירמיה בר אבא says that רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן argue only about the extra-rejoicing music of the Water Drawing. A ברייתא and then the משנה refute רב יוסף on both counts: the dispute is about the Water Drawing, and everyone agrees the music of the קרבן overrides שבת. The גמרא then gives each side's verse for בפה or בכלי, and each side explains away the other's verse. Finally, a new משנה describes the glorious שמחת בית השואבה: giant golden מנורות, wicks from the כהנים' old clothes, light filling all of ירושלים, and חסידים dancing before the crowd.

steps.title: A tannaitic dispute about who the Temple musicians were
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the earlier argument has a parallel among תנאים. It quotes three opinions about who played the instruments in the מקדש: slaves of כהנים, distinguished Israelite families, or לוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים, as it was taught: They were slaves of כהנים, says רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי says: they were from the family of בית הפגרים and the family of בית ציפריא, from the town of אמאום, and their lineage was so good that their daughters married כהנים. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: they were לוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה (in מסכת ערכין) with three opinions about who played the instruments in the מקדש. It is setting up the next step, where it will try to link this dispute to the earlier argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כתנאי tells us the גמרא wants to show that the earlier argument (בפה or בכלי) already exists among תנאים. There are three positions: slaves (low status), distinguished Israelites (יחוס but not לוים), and לוים (the tribe whose job is Temple song). At this point the גמרא has not yet explained why they argue; the next step proposes a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: This is like a dispute of the תנאים, a parallel tannaitic argument
They married their daughters to כהנים, a sign of pure lineage
Members of the tribe of לוי, who did the Temple song

steps.confusionAlert: This dispute is about the people who played the instruments, not the singers. Everyone knows the singing itself was done by the לוים.

phrases.english: It is like a dispute of tanna'im, as it was taught:
They (the instrument players) were slaves of priests,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yosei says:
The family of the House of Happegarim
and the family of the House of Tzipperaya,
and they were from Emma'um,
who would marry their daughters into the priesthood.
Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says:
They were Levites.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the earlier argument over בפה or בכלי (on the previous amud) to a dispute of תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three tannaitic views on the instrument players: slaves of כהנים (רבי מאיר), distinguished Israelite families (רבי יוסי), לוים (רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס).

steps.title: Suggesting the dispute depends on singing versus instruments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the one who says slaves played holds עיקר שירה בפה, and the one who says לוים played holds עיקר שירה בכלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that they argue about this? The one who says they were slaves holds that the main part of the song is the singing voice. The one who says they were לוים holds that the main part of the song is the instruments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes the reason behind the tannaitic dispute. It ties it to the question of whether the voice or the instruments are the main part of the Temple song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the singing is the real עבודה, the instruments are only background, so anyone, even slaves, may play them. If the instruments are the real עבודה, they are part of the Levite service, so only לוים may play. This would make the earlier argument a dispute of תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (a formula that proposes an explanation)
The main part of the Temple song
With the mouth, meaning the singing voice

steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whether the voice or the instrument is primary decides whether instrument playing counts as real עבודה that needs לוים.

phrases.english: Is it not that they argue about this:
that the one who said they were slaves
holds: the main part of song is with the mouth.
And the one who said they were Levites
holds: the main part of song is with the instrument.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a reason for the dispute quoted in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the dispute over בפה or בכלי already exists among תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in ערכין of רבי מאיר and רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס (slaves versus לוים)

steps.title: רבי יוסי's view fits neither side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion: רבי יוסי's view (distinguished Israelites) does not fit בפה, which would allow even slaves, and does not fit בכלי, which would require לוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think so? What does רבי יוסי hold? If he holds the main part of song is the voice, then even slaves should be fine. If he holds the main part is the instrument, then only לוים, not Israelites!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from step 2. It shows that the middle opinion, רבי יוסי's, makes no sense under either side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under בפה, the instruments are just background, so why does רבי יוסי insist on families with fine יחוס? Even slaves would do. Under בכלי, playing is Levite work, so Israelites, however distinguished, should not be allowed. Since רבי יוסי fits neither, the proposed link must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really think so? (introduces a strong objection)
If ... and if: setting up both options

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי's families are Israelites, not לוים. That is why the בכלי option fails for him.

phrases.english: And can you understand it that way?!
What does Rabbi Yosei hold?
If he holds the main part of song is with the mouth,
then even slaves would also be acceptable;
if he holds the main part of song is with the instrument,
then Levites yes, Israelites no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation proposed in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the tannaitic dispute depends on עיקר שירה בפה or בכלי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: רבי יוסי's requirement of distinguished Israelites fits neither בפה, which would allow even slaves, nor בכלי, which would allow only לוים.

steps.title: Everyone agrees singing is primary; the dispute is only historical
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the link: all agree עיקר שירה בפה, and the תנאים only disagree about what actually happened, meaning who in fact played the instruments.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees the main part of the song is the voice. They argue about this: one Sage says this is how it actually was, and the other Sage says this is how it actually was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reading of the משנה in ערכין. It is not a legal argument at all, only a disagreement about historical fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since all hold בפה, anyone could legally play the instruments. The תנאים are only reporting different memories of who actually did play: slaves, fine Israelite families, or לוים. So the attempt (כתנאי) to find the earlier argument among תנאים is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: One Sage holds ... and the other Sage holds
This is how the event happened, a factual report

steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to tie the בפה or בכלי argument to the תנאים fails. All three תנאים agree עיקר שירה בפה. They only disagree about history, about who actually played the instruments in the מקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move: a dispute that looks legal can be read as a disagreement over facts. That leaves רב יוסף's explanation of the earlier dispute (בפה versus בכלי) without support from this משנה.

phrases.english: Rather: that everyone agrees
the main part of song is with the mouth.
And about this they argue:
that one Sage holds: this is how the event was,
and the other Sage holds: this is how the event was.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא עִיקַּר שִׁירָה בַּפֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 by giving up the explanation from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the dispute is about historical fact, not law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים disagree about whether the voice or the instruments are primary.
steps.terutzMaskana: All agree עיקר שירה בפה. The dispute is only about who actually played the instruments.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The כתנאי is rejected. The tannaitic dispute over the musicians is a historical disagreement, and everyone holds עיקר שירה בפה.

steps.title: What practical difference does it make who played?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is in arguing over who actually played the instruments.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has just said the תנאים only argue about a historical fact. Now it asks why that fact matters in practice, which sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An argument about history alone seems pointless. The גמרא wants to find a real halachic result that depends on who played the instruments.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the practical result of the answer given in step 4, that the dispute is only about what actually happened.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What halachic result depends on who actually played the instruments in the מקדש.

steps.title: The difference: proving lineage and tithe rights from the platform
steps.stepSummary: The תנאים disagree about whether serving on the דוכן proves pure lineage and the right to receive מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about whether we raise someone from the platform to lineage status and to tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the practical difference is about family status. If we know a man's ancestor played on the דוכן, what can we conclude about his family?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only certain people were allowed to play, then having played proves the family belongs to that group. Two things might be proven this way: pure lineage, meaning the family may marry into כהונה, and being a לוי, meaning the family receives מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: We raise, meaning we grant a presumed status
The platform where the לוים sang and played

phrases.english: Regarding whether we raise someone from the platform
to lineage status and to tithes, that is what they disagree about.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַעֲלִין מִדּוּכָן לְיוּחֲסִין וּלְמַעֲשֵׂר קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The practical difference is whether playing on the דוכן serves as proof of pure lineage and of the right to מעשר.

steps.title: How each of the three views rules on lineage and tithes
steps.stepSummary: Slaves view: no proof at all. Israelites view: proof of lineage but not of tithes. לוים view: proof of both.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says they were slaves holds that we do not raise someone from the platform to lineage status or to tithes. The one who says they were Israelites holds that we do raise someone from the platform to lineage status, but not to tithes. The one who says they were לוים holds that we raise someone from the platform both to lineage status and to tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through each opinion and shows what it concludes about a person who played on the דוכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even slaves could play, playing proves nothing. If only distinguished Israelite families played, it proves pure lineage but not that the man is a לוי, so he gets no מעשר. If only לוים played, it proves both that he is a לוי and that his lineage is pure.
steps.whatToRemember: Each answer to "who played?" decides what playing on the דוכן proves: nothing (slaves), lineage only (Israelites), or lineage and מעשר (לוים).

phrases.english: The one who said they were slaves holds:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַעֲלִין מִדּוּכָן לְיוּחֲסִין, וְלֹא לְמַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: we do not raise from the platform to lineage status, nor to tithes.
And the one who said they were Israelites holds:
we raise from the platform to lineage status,
but not to tithes.
And the one who said they were Levites holds:
we raise from the platform
both to lineage status and to tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the general answer of step 6 for each of the three opinions from step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Slaves: no status proven. Israelites: lineage proven, but not מעשר. לוים: both lineage and מעשר proven.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה בר אבא: the dispute is about the music of the Water Drawing
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא says the dispute between רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן is about the music of שמחת בית השואבה. Everyone agrees the music of the קרבן overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: The dispute is about the music of the Water Drawing. רבי יוסי בר יהודה holds that extra rejoicing also overrides שבת, and the רבנן hold that extra rejoicing does not override שבת. But regarding the music of the קרבן, everyone agrees it is part of the עבודה and overrides שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier dispute between רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן. It brings רבי ירמיה בר אבא, who explains it differently from רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף had said they argue about the music of the קרבן, and that the argument depends on whether עיקר שירה בכלי. רבי ירמיה moves the argument to the music of the Water Drawing celebration. The real question becomes whether extra rejoicing, which is not part of the עבודה itself, overrides שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The music at the celebration of the Water Drawing
Extra rejoicing, beyond what the service requires
The song that accompanies the קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of music. The song of the קרבן is part of the עבודה and overrides שבת according to everyone here. The argument is only about the extra celebration music of the Water Drawing.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
The dispute is about the song of the Water Drawing,
for Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda holds:

phrases.aramaic: שִׂמְחָה יְתֵירָה נָמֵי דּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: extra rejoicing also overrides Shabbat,
and the Rabbis hold:

phrases.aramaic: שִׂמְחָה יְתֵירָה אֵינָהּ דּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: extra rejoicing does not override Shabbat.
But regarding the song of the offering,
everyone agrees it is part of the service,
and it overrides Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּשִׁיר שֶׁל שׁוֹאֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the תנאים digression and offers a different reading from רב יוסף's (stated earlier) of the dispute between רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute concerns the music of the Water Drawing: does extra rejoicing override שבת? The music of the קרבן is עבודה and overrides שבת according to everyone.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the dispute is about the Water Drawing music
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says explicitly that רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the חכמים argue about the music of the Water Drawing. This challenges רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: The music of the Water Drawing overrides שבת; these are the words of רבי יוסי בר יהודה. And the חכמים say: It does not even override יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to challenge רב יוסף. The ברייתא openly names the music of the Water Drawing as the subject of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said the argument is about the music of the קרבן. But the ברייתא presents the same two parties arguing about the Water Drawing music, exactly as רבי ירמיה בר אבא said. The חכמים here even hold it does not override יום טוב, so it is clearly not treated as עבודה.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁיר שֶׁל שׁוֹאֵבָה דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: The song of the Water Drawing overrides Shabbat,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda.
And the Sages say:
It does not override even the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that matches רבי ירמיה בר אבא's reading in step 8 and contradicts רב יוסף.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן argue about the music of the קרבן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא states outright that the subject of their argument is the music of the Water Drawing, not the music of the קרבן.

steps.title: רב יוסף is conclusively refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that this is a refutation of רב יוסף and confirms that it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this a refutation of רב יוסף? Yes, it is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states that the ברייתא refutes רב יוסף and accepts that conclusion. No answer is offered for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תיובתא means the view cannot stand. On this point the dispute is about the music of the Water Drawing, as רבי ירמיה בר אבא said. Whether everyone also agrees that the music of the קרבן overrides שבת is argued in the next steps: step 12 defends רב יוסף on that point, and step 14 settles it.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף is refuted on his first claim: the ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן argue about the extra-rejoicing music of the Water Drawing. Whether the music of the קרבן overrides שבת according to all is taken up in steps 11-14.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Rav Yosef!
Indeed, it is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the challenge in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יוסף's reading is rejected. The dispute is about the music of the Water Drawing, as רבי ירמיה בר אבא said.

steps.title: Suggesting a double refutation of רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא implies the dispute is only about the Water Drawing music, and that everyone agrees the קרבן music overrides שבת. That would refute רב יוסף on two points.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say they disagree only about the song of the Water Drawing, but about the song of the קרבן everyone agrees it overrides שבת. If so, this is a refutation of רב יוסף on two counts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the ברייתא one step further. It suggests that it does not just challenge one point of רב יוסף's view but two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said two things. First, the dispute is about the קרבן music. Second, everyone agrees the Water Drawing music does not override שבת. If the dispute is really only about the Water Drawing, and the קרבן music overrides שבת according to all, then both of his claims fall.

keyTerms.meaning: The music played with the daily offering

steps.confusionAlert: "Two counts" means two separate claims of רב יוסף. One is about where the dispute lies, and the other is that the רבנן say the קרבן music does not override שבת. Both are now under attack.

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא בְּשִׁיר שֶׁל שׁוֹאֵבָה הוּא דִּפְלִיגִי,
phrases.english: Let us say it is about the song of the Water Drawing that they disagree,
but regarding the song of the offering,
all agree it overrides Shabbat.
Let us say this is a refutation
of Rav Yosef on two counts!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בְּתַרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ברייתא's challenge to cover a second point of רב יוסף's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's view that the dispute is about the קרבן music and that the Water Drawing music does not override שבת according to all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the ברייתא names the Water Drawing as the topic of the dispute, it implies the קרבן music overrides שבת according to everyone. That contradicts both claims of רב יוסף.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the dispute covers both kinds of music
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that they argue about both the Water Drawing and the קרבן music. The ברייתא mentions the Water Drawing only to show how far רבי יוסי בר יהודה goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף can say: they disagree about the Water Drawing song, and the same applies to the קרבן song. They mention the Water Drawing to show the strength of רבי יוסי בר יהודה's view: even the Water Drawing music overrides שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף against the second count ("אמר לך רב יוסף", meaning רב יוסף could say to you). The ברייתא does not exclude the קרבן music from the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף reads the dispute as covering both cases. The ברייתא names the more extreme case, the Water Drawing, to show that רבי יוסי בר יהודה permits even that on שבת. So the ברייתא does not prove that everyone agrees about the קרבן music.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you (introduces a defense)
To let you know the strength (how far a view goes)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef could say to you:
They disagree about the song of the Water Drawing,
and the same is true for the offering.
And the fact that they disagree about the song of the Water Drawing

phrases.aramaic: לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחוֹ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: is to let you know how far Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda goes,
that even the Water Drawing music also overrides Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Deflects the second count of the refutation suggested in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why the ברייתא chose its example (כחו דהיתרא, showing the strength of the lenient view).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא names only the Water Drawing, so the קרבן music must be agreed upon by all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute covers both. The Water Drawing is named to show the extreme reach of רבי יוסי בר יהודה's leniency.

steps.title: The משנה implies the offering flute overrides שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the Water Drawing flute does not override שבת. This implies the קרבן flute does. That cannot be רבי יוסי בר יהודה, so it must be the רבנן, which refutes רב יוסף on two counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches: this is the flute of the Water Drawing, which overrides neither שבת nor יום טוב. So this one does not override, but the קרבן flute does. Whose view is this? It cannot be רבי יוסי בר יהודה, since he says even the Water Drawing music overrides. So it must be the רבנן, and רב יוסף is refuted on two counts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, the משנה, to knock down רב יוסף's defense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stresses that "this" flute does not override שבת, which implies that the קרבן flute does. That fits only the רבנן, since רבי יוסי בר יהודה permits even the Water Drawing music. So the רבנן agree the קרבן instrument overrides שבת, against רב יוסף, and they disagree with רבי יוסי בר יהודה about the Water Drawing, also against רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught? (introduces a contradicting source)
The place or celebration of the Water Drawing

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
This is the flute of the Place of the Water Drawing

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינוֹ דּוֹחֶה לֹא אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא אֶת יוֹם טוֹב:
phrases.english: which overrides neither Shabbat nor Yom Tov:
this is the one that does not override,
but the flute of the offering does override.

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּי? אִי נֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Whose view is this? If we say Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: הָאָמַר שִׁיר שֶׁל שׁוֹאֵבָה נָמֵי דּוֹחֶה!
phrases.english: didn't he say that the Water Drawing song also overrides?!
Rather, is it not the Rabbis?
And this is a refutation of Rav Yosef on two counts!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's defense from step 12 by using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the רבנן say the קרבן instrument does not override שבת, and that the dispute is not about the Water Drawing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's inference (the קרבן flute overrides שבת) must follow the רבנן. So the רבנן permit the קרבן instrument on שבת, and the two sides differ only about the Water Drawing.

steps.title: רב יוסף is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב יוסף is indeed refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge as final. רב יוסף's view is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No further defense is offered. The view of רבי ירמיה בר אבא stands: the dispute is about the Water Drawing music, and everyone agrees the קרבן music overrides שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Final result: רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן argue only about the music of שמחת בית השואבה. Everyone agrees that the music of the קרבן overrides שבת.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the refutation raised in step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יוסף is refuted on both counts. The קרבן music overrides שבת according to all, and the dispute is only about the Water Drawing.

steps.title: Asking for the source that the main song is instrumental
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the view that the main part of the Temple song is the instrument.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the one who says the main part of the song is with an instrument?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It is setting up a question about the source for the view that instruments are the essence of the Temple song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא mentioned a view that the essence of the Levites' song is the instrumental music, not the singing voice. Now it asks where that view comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The main part of the song is with an instrument

phrases.english: What is the reason
of the one who says the main part of the song is with an instrument?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר עִיקַּר שִׁירָה בִּכְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the רב יוסף discussion, the גמרא turns to the scriptural basis of a related view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse or reasoning behind the view עיקר שירה בכלי.

steps.title: The verse about חזקיהו's offering
steps.stepSummary: The source is a verse in דברי הימים: when the עולה began, the song of ה׳ began with trumpets and the instruments of דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And חזקיהו said to offer the עולה on the altar, and when the עולה began, the song of ה׳ began, with the trumpets and the instruments of דוד king of Israel."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a פסוק that links the "song of ה׳" to musical instruments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse calls the music "the song of ה׳" and connects it directly to the trumpets and the instruments of דוד. This shows that the instruments are central to the Temple song, which supports the view עיקר שירה בכלי.

keyTerms.meaning: The song of ה׳ (the Temple song)

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And Hezekiah said to offer the burnt-offering on the altar,
and when the burnt-offering began,
the song of the Lord began, and the trumpets,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל יְדֵי כְּלֵי דָּוִיד מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל״.
phrases.english: together with the instruments of David, king of Israel."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 with a verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse in דברי הימים links "the song of ה׳" to the trumpets and the instruments of דוד, showing that the instrument is the essence of the song.

steps.title: What is the source for the view that the main song is with the mouth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks for the source of the opposite view: that the main part of the song is the singing voice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for the one who says that the main part of the song is with the mouth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא already gave the source for the instrument view. Now it asks for the source of the other view, the voice view, and sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 15-16 gave a verse for 'the main song is the instrument.' To be fair to both sides, the גמרא now asks what verse supports 'the main song is the mouth.'

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (a certain opinion)
The main part of the song is with the mouth (singing voice)

phrases.english: What is the reason of the one who says
the main part of the song is with the mouth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 15, now asking about the opposite opinion
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the view that the main song is with the mouth

steps.title: The source: trumpeters and singers made one sound
steps.stepSummary: The voice view learns from a verse that puts the trumpeters and the singers together as one sound, and lists no other instruments with the singers.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And it was as one, for the trumpeters and the singers, to make one sound heard.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a verse in דברי הימים that talks about singers making a sound, without listing musical instruments with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse calls the musicians 'singers' (משוררים), meaning people who sing with their voices. The only instruments mentioned are trumpets, which were blown for the קרבן and not as background music for the song. So the song itself is the voice.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And it was as one,
for the trumpeters and for the singers,
to make one sound heard.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse about trumpeters and singers making one sound shows that the song is the singers' voices

steps.title: Challenge to the voice view from the חזקיהו verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the voice view: what about the verse about חזקיהו, which mentions the instruments of דוד?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too: isn't it written 'And חזקיהו said' (that verse which mentions instruments)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the voice view with the verse that the instrument view used in step 16. The voice view must explain that verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חזקיהו verse says the song of ה׳ began 'with the instruments of דוד.' This sounds like the instruments are the main part, so how can the voice view ignore it?

keyTerms.meaning: And the other side too (how does it explain this?)
King חזקיהו, who restored the Temple service

phrases.english: And the other one too,
isn't it written: 'And Hezekiah said'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the instrument view's verse against the voice view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חזקיהו verse links the song to the instruments of דוד, which suggests the instrument is the main part

steps.title: The instruments were only to sweeten the voice
steps.stepSummary: The voice view reads the verse in two parts: the song began with the mouth, and the instruments of דוד were added just to make the sound sweeter.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the verse means: 'The song of ה׳ began' with the mouth; 'through the instruments of דוד, king of ישראל' to sweeten the sound.
steps.whatsHappening: The voice view answers the challenge by splitting the verse. The singing is the main thing, and the instruments are only background music.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'the song of ה׳ began' refer to singing with the mouth. The words 'with the instruments of דוד' do not describe the main song. They only describe extra music that made the singing sound nicer.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
'The song of ה׳ began' with the mouth;
'through the instruments of David, king of Israel'
is to sweeten the sound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the verse: splitting it into a main part and an extra part
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse makes the instruments the heart of the song
steps.terutzMaskana: The singing is the song; the instruments only make it sound better

steps.title: Challenge to the instrument view from the 'one sound' verse
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא asks the instrument view: what about the verse that calls them singers making one sound?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too: isn't it written 'And it was as one, for the trumpeters and the singers'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns around and challenges the instrument view with the voice view's verse from step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That verse speaks of 'singers' (משוררים), which sounds like voices. So how can the instrument view say the main song is the instrument?

phrases.english: And the other one too, isn't it written:
'And it was as one, for the trumpeters and for the singers'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of step 19, now aimed at the instrument view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse mentions 'singers,' which implies voices are the main song

steps.title: Singers are compared to trumpeters: both use instruments
steps.stepSummary: The instrument view says the verse puts singers next to trumpeters to teach that, just like trumpeters, the singers also used instruments.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the verse means: the singers are like the trumpeters. Just as trumpeters use an instrument, so too the singers use an instrument.
steps.whatsHappening: The instrument view answers by reading the verse as a comparison. Because the singers and trumpeters are listed together, they work the same way, with instruments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The voice view saw the word 'singers' as a sign of voices. The instrument view says the important point is that the two groups are placed side by side 'as one.' Trumpeters clearly use instruments, so the singers did too. Each side has now explained away the other side's verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as ... so too ... (a comparison formula)

steps.whatToRemember: Each side has its own verse and explains the other's verse. Voice view: the instruments only sweeten the singing. Instrument view: the singers are like trumpeters, so they also played instruments.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
singers are like trumpeters;
just as trumpeters are with an instrument,
so too singers are with an instrument.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 and closes the dispute
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison drawn from placing two groups side by side in the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Singers' means people singing with their voices
steps.terutzMaskana: The singers are compared to the trumpeters, so they also used instruments

steps.title: No one has seen real joy without seeing שמחת בית השואבה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens with a famous line: whoever did not see שמחת בית השואבה never saw true joy.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Whoever did not see the celebration of בית השואבה never saw joy in his life.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It opens by praising שמחת בית השואבה as the greatest joy there ever was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line sets the tone for everything the משנה will describe next. The celebration was held on the nights of סוכות, connected to drawing the water for ניסוך המים, the water offering poured on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: The celebration of the place of water drawing, held on סוכות nights

steps.confusionAlert: The name sounds like it is only about drawing water, but the משנה goes on to describe lights, dancing, and music. The celebration is named for the water offering it honors, not because the party was at the well.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who did not see
the celebration of the Place of the Water Drawing
never saw joy in his days.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה שִׂמְחַת בֵּית הַשּׁוֹאֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה; a new topic begins
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמחת בית השואבה was the greatest joy ever seen

steps.title: The setup in עזרת נשים: golden מנורות, ladders, and young כהנים
steps.stepSummary: After the first day of סוכות, they went down to עזרת נשים, made a big arrangement, and set up huge golden מנורות that young כהנים filled with oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the end of the first day of יום טוב of the חג, they went down to עזרת נשים and made a great arrangement there. Golden מנורות stood there, with four golden basins on top of each. Each one had four ladders, and four young כהנים held jugs of 120 לוג of oil, which they poured into each basin.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes how the celebration was set up: where it happened and how the giant lights were prepared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'great arrangement' (תיקון גדול) will be explained by the גמרא; it was a change made to keep men and women apart. The מנורות were so tall that ladders were needed to reach the basins, and young כהנים climbed up to pour in the oil.

keyTerms.meaning: The night after יום טוב ends
The Women's Courtyard in the בית המקדש
A great arrangement (explained later in the גמרא)

phrases.aramaic: בְּמוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג
phrases.english: At the end of the first Yom Tov of the festival
they went down to the Women's Courtyard,
and they made a great arrangement there.
Golden candelabra were there,
and four golden basins on their tops,
and four ladders for each and every one,
and four youths from the young priests,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִידֵיהֶם כַּדִּים שֶׁל מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים לוֹג
phrases.english: and in their hands jugs of 120 log
which they pour into each and every basin.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by describing the setup
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giant golden מנורות were set up in עזרת נשים and filled with oil by young כהנים

steps.title: Wicks from the כהנים' old clothes lit up all of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The wicks were made from worn-out pants and belts of the כהנים, and the light was so strong that every courtyard in ירושלים was lit.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the worn-out pants of the כהנים and from their belts they would tear strips, and with them they would light. There was no courtyard in ירושלים that was not lit by the light of בית השואבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the description: it tells what the wicks were made of and how bright the light was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even old, worn-out clothing of the כהנים was put to holy use as wicks. The closing line shows the size of the celebration: its light reached every home in ירושלים.
steps.whatToRemember: שמחת בית השואבה was a nighttime celebration in עזרת נשים, lit by giant golden מנורות whose wicks came from the כהנים' old clothes, and its light filled all of ירושלים.

phrases.english: From the worn-out trousers of the priests and from their belts,
from them they would tear strips,
and with them they would light.
And there was no courtyard in Jerusalem
that was not lit by the light of the Place of the Water Drawing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה's description of the lighting
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wicks came from the old clothes of the כהנים, and the light reached every courtyard in ירושלים

steps.title: The Pious Men Danced Before the Crowd
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues describing שמחת בית השואבה: the חסידים and אנשי מעשה danced in front of the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: The very pious people and the men of good deeds would dance in front of everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps describing the celebration and tells us who did the dancing. It was the most righteous people, the חסידים and אנשי מעשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After describing the setting, the golden מנורות and the light that filled ירושלים, the משנה now describes the people at the event. The dancers were not ordinary entertainers. They were the greatest and most pious people, and they danced to lead the crowd in joy. This shows that the celebration was a holy act of עבודת ה׳, not just a party.

keyTerms.meaning: Very pious people who go beyond what the law requires
Men of good deeds. Some explain it as people known for righteous actions, or even as people who could perform wonders.
In front of them, meaning the crowd watching

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the dancers were hired performers or young people having fun. The משנה stresses that the holiest people danced. That is exactly why this joy was so special.

phrases.english: The pious and the men of good deeds
phrases.notes: The greatest and most righteous people of the generation

phrases.english: would dance before them
phrases.notes: "Them" refers to the people who came to watch the celebration

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲסִידִים וְאַנְשֵׁי מַעֲשֶׂה הָיוּ מְרַקְּדִין בִּפְנֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of שמחת בית השואבה. It moves from the lighting setup to the people who led the dancing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At שמחת בית השואבה, the חסידים and אנשי מעשה personally danced before the assembled people.
